course.title: Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring
course.tagline: Take a trained model from a notebook to a versioned, containerised, monitored service, size it against a latency objective, and release and roll it back on evidence
course.description: Participants take two trained models from a notebook to a monitored service. For a fictional mutual insurer they package a claims-triage classifier and a similar-claims embedding model with pinned dependencies, register model versions, serve them behind a versioned API with input validation, build and scan a container image, run it on a single-node local cluster with health checks, add metrics, structured logs and traces, load-test and size the service, release a new version by canary and roll it back, and detect drift in a replayed stream of claims.
course.audience: Practitioners. Graduates and early-career developers who have completed the FN courses or passed the placement test, and software engineers moving into AI work.
prerequisites: FN-102 Command Line, Git and Reproducible Projects
AE-201 Machine Learning Foundations and Model Evaluation
Runs commands in a Linux shell
Has trained a model and saved it to a file
course.format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

outcomes.text: Explain the path from a trained model to a served prediction, naming the artefact, image, registry, runtime, endpoint and monitor at each step, given a deployment diagram with the components unlabelled
outcomes.evidence: a labelled diagram with a one-sentence role for each component, scored against the reference

outcomes.text: Prepare a model artefact with pinned dependencies, a version, an input and output signature and a reproducible build, given a trained model and its training script
outcomes.evidence: a registered model version that a fresh environment loads and that reproduces ten reference predictions

outcomes.text: Implement a versioned prediction API with input validation, typed errors and separate health and readiness checks, given the registered model and an API contract
outcomes.evidence: a passing contract test suite, including malformed inputs and a model file that fails to load

outcomes.text: Configure a container image for the service, scan it for vulnerabilities and run it with resource limits on a single-node cluster, given the service code and a base image
outcomes.evidence: an image under a stated size, a scan report with no critical findings and a deployment that passes its readiness check

outcomes.text: Implement metrics, structured logs and traces for the service and a dashboard for latency percentiles, error rate and prediction distribution, given the running service and a load generator
outcomes.evidence: a dashboard defined as code and an alert rule that fires on a seeded error spike

outcomes.text: Measure latency and throughput under load and size workers and replicas to meet a latency objective at the lowest cost, given a target request rate and a 95th-percentile latency objective set by the insurer, on laptop CPUs
outcomes.evidence: a load-test report with the chosen configuration and its cost per 1,000 predictions

outcomes.text: Deliver a new model version by canary release, decide on promotion or rollback from monitored metrics and detect drift in replayed traffic, given two model versions, four weeks of replayed claims with injected drift and written rollback criteria
outcomes.evidence: a release log with the decision and its evidence, a completed rollback and a drift report naming the shifted features

case_study.name: Rifd Mutual Insurance
case_study.summary: Rifd Mutual Insurance is a fictional cooperative insurer whose claims team wants two notebook models in service: Farz, which triages each new motor, health or property claim, and Shabih, which finds similar past claims for an adjuster. Every lab works on 50,000 synthetic claims made by a seeded generator, the models the kit trains on a laptop processor, and four weeks of replayed claims with drift injected from the third week; the personal fields in the data are invented.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: Package and serve
days.subtitle: From a notebook pickle to a versioned API that checks its inputs and says when it is ready

sessions.label: Session 1
sessions.title: From notebook to artefact
sessions.summary: The path from a trained model to a served prediction, serialisation formats, signatures, pins and the decision logic that hides in a notebook
outcomes: Name the artefact, image, registry, runtime, endpoint and monitor on a deployment path
Convert a notebook pickle into an artefact with a signature, pins and its decision rule
Prove an artefact by reloading it in a clean environment against reference predictions

lab.title: Export Farz as an artefact
lab.summary: Export the claims-triage model with its signature and pinned dependencies and reload it in a clean environment, reproducing ten reference predictions.

steps.text: Build the workspace and open lab 1.1
Load the notebook pickle and read what it needs
Export with a signature, pins and the decision rule
Reload in a clean environment; match ten predictions
Check

lab.stretch: Open the pickle with pickletools and list the imports it would run on load

sessions.label: Session 2
sessions.title: A registry for model versions
sessions.summary: Immutable versions with metrics, tags and lineage, aliases for champion and challenger, and loading by version
outcomes: Register a model version with metrics, a data hash and a commit
Explain why a registered version is never overwritten
Load a model by version and by alias and say when to use each

lab.title: Register two versions
lab.summary: Register two supplied model versions with metrics and tags and load one by version.

steps.text: Read the two supplied artefacts and their metrics
Register 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 with tags and a data hash
Try to overwrite 1.0.0 and read the refusal
Set the champion alias; load by version and by alias
Check

lab.stretch: Write the same two registrations as MLflow calls, or as git tags on an artefact repository

sessions.label: Session 3
sessions.title: A prediction API with a contract
sessions.summary: Online, batch and streaming prediction, a contract written first, input validation, typed errors and a version in the path
outcomes: Choose online, batch or streaming prediction for a use case
Validate a request against a written contract before the model sees it
Return typed errors that a caller can act on

lab.title: A versioned endpoint with a contract
lab.summary: Build a versioned prediction endpoint that validates inputs and returns typed errors, until the supplied contract tests pass.

steps.text: Run the contract tests against the naive endpoint
Write the request and response schemas
Return problem details for each error type
Pass all contract tests
Check

lab.stretch: Add a batch endpoint that takes up to 100 claims and reports errors per item

sessions.label: Session 4
sessions.title: Health, readiness and warm-up
sessions.summary: Liveness and readiness as two questions, loading and warming the model at start, and what a service does when its model file is missing
outcomes: Separate a liveness check from a readiness check
Load and warm a model before the service accepts traffic
Show the behaviour of each check when the model file fails to load

lab.title: Health and readiness checks
lab.summary: Add health and readiness checks and show how they differ when the model file is missing.

steps.text: See the old health check say OK with no model
Load and warm the model in the lifespan
Write /livez and /readyz
Test both with the model file missing
Check

lab.stretch: Make /readyz fail when the warm-up prediction disagrees with the artefact's reference prediction

days.label: Day 2
days.title: Containers and a cluster
days.subtitle: An image that is small, scanned and configured from outside, running on a local cluster

sessions.label: Session 1
sessions.title: Images that are small and reproducible
sessions.summary: Layers and the build cache, multi-stage builds from the lock file, slim bases, a non-root user and what to leave out
outcomes: Read a container file and predict which layers a change rebuilds
Write a multi-stage container file that installs from the lock file
Measure image size and build time and explain the difference

lab.title: A multi-stage container file
lab.summary: Write a multi-stage container file and compare its size and build time with a naive one.

steps.text: Build the naive image; record size and time
Write the multi-stage file without AI help
Build it; record size, time and a rebuild after a code change
Check

lab.stretch: Pin the base image by digest and rebuild twice: do the two images have the same id?

sessions.label: Session 2
sessions.title: Scanning and configuration
sessions.summary: What a scanner reads and reports, severities and fixed versions, secrets in image layers, and configuration from the environment
outcomes: Read a vulnerability report and pick the finding to fix first
Fix a finding by moving to a fixed version and scan again
Move a secret out of an image into configuration the runtime supplies

lab.title: Scan, fix, configure
lab.summary: Scan a supplied image, fix one critical finding and move secrets out of the image into configuration.

steps.text: Scan the supplied image and read the report
Fix the critical finding and scan again
Find the key in the image history
Read the key from configuration instead
Check

lab.stretch: Scan the multi-stage image of lab 2.1 and compare the counts by severity

sessions.label: Session 3
sessions.title: Running on a local cluster
sessions.summary: Deployments, services and probes, requests and limits, rolling updates, and where a service may run under data rules
outcomes: Deploy a service with probes and resource limits to a single-node cluster
Diagnose a pod that does not become ready from its events
Decide where each service may run from its data classification

lab.title: Deploy to a local cluster
lab.summary: Deploy the supplied service image to a single-node cluster with probes and resource limits, and decide where each service may run.

steps.text: Create the cluster and load the image
Apply the supplied manifest; read why it fails
Add probes, limits and a pinned image
Fill the placement table for three services
Check

lab.stretch: Change the image tag and watch a rolling update replace the pods one at a time

sessions.label: Session 4
sessions.title: Serving the embedding model
sessions.summary: An embedding model as a service: vectors and an index in memory, start-up time, a startup probe and a deployment of its own
outcomes: Serve a nearest-neighbour search behind a versioned endpoint
Measure memory and time to ready for two models
Decide whether two models share a deployment

lab.title: The similar-claims endpoint
lab.summary: Add the similar-claims endpoint and compare its memory use and start-up time with the classifier.

steps.text: Read the Shabih artefact and its index
Add /v1/similar with a contract and no personal fields
Measure memory and time to ready for both models
Check

lab.stretch: Halve the index with float16 vectors and measure what it saves and what it changes in the results

days.label: Day 3
days.title: Observe and size
days.subtitle: Metrics, logs and traces that answer questions, then the load the service can carry and what it costs

sessions.label: Session 1
sessions.title: Metrics that matter
sessions.summary: Rate, errors and duration, histograms and their buckets, percentiles, the distribution of predictions and dashboards defined as code
outcomes: Instrument a service with request, error and latency metrics
Compute the 50th, 95th and 99th percentiles from histogram buckets
Define a dashboard as code with latency, errors and predictions

lab.title: Rate, errors and latency
lab.summary: Expose request rate, error rate and latency histograms and graph the 50th, 95th and 99th percentiles.

steps.text: Add the counters and the latency histogram
Add the prediction distribution
Drive traffic and compute the percentiles
Read the dashboard file; check

lab.stretch: Move the histogram buckets and see how far the estimated 95th percentile moves

sessions.label: Session 2
sessions.title: Logs and traces
sessions.summary: Structured logs with a request id, personal fields redacted at the edge, and traces that show where one slow request spent its time
outcomes: Write one structured log line per request with a request id
Redact personal fields before they reach a log or a trace, and test it
Follow one slow request through its spans to the slow step

lab.title: Logs, redaction and a trace
lab.summary: Add structured logs with a request id, redact personal fields and follow one slow request through a trace.

steps.text: Find the personal fields in the current logs
Log JSON with a request id; redact at the edge
Add spans; find the slowest request and its slow span
Check

lab.stretch: Pass the request id to the policy lookup as a header and see it in the lookup's own log

sessions.label: Session 3
sessions.title: Load testing
sessions.summary: Open and closed load, warm-up, steady rates, percentiles under load and the knee where latency breaks the objective
outcomes: Write a load test that sends realistic requests at a fixed rate
Run it at three rates and read percentiles, errors and throughput
Locate the rate at which the 95th percentile breaks the objective

lab.title: Three rates against the objective
lab.summary: Run a load test at three request rates and find where latency breaks the objective.

steps.text: Read the objective and the locust file
Make the requests realistic
Run three rates with a warm-up
Report where the objective breaks; check

lab.stretch: Run the same rates with k6 and compare the two tools' numbers

sessions.label: Session 4
sessions.title: Sizing and cost
sessions.summary: Workers and replicas, concurrency on a processor, headroom, processor against graphics-processor serving and the cost of 1,000 predictions
outcomes: Measure the rate one worker carries within the objective
Choose workers and replicas for a target rate with headroom
Compute the cost per 1,000 predictions of a configuration

lab.title: Workers, replicas and cost
lab.summary: Tune workers and replicas to meet the latency objective and compute cost per 1,000 predictions.

steps.text: Measure one, two and four workers at the target rate
Choose workers and replicas with headroom
Compute cost per 1,000 predictions
Check

lab.stretch: Price the same load on the cheapest configuration that breaks the objective and say what Munira would lose

days.label: Day 4
days.title: Release and watch
days.subtitle: Release a new version on evidence, roll back a bad one, watch the inputs drift and hand over to the on-call engineer

sessions.label: Session 1
sessions.title: Rolling, canary and shadow releases
sessions.summary: Blue-green, rolling, canary and shadow releases, and comparing a canary with the current version on the same metrics
outcomes: Choose a release strategy for a change and its risk
Send a fixed share of traffic to a new version
Compare two versions on errors, latency and predictions

lab.title: A 10% canary
lab.summary: Send 10% of traffic to a new version and compare its metrics with the current one.

steps.text: Start both versions and the router
Replay claims with 10% to the canary
Compare errors, latency and predictions
Write the release log entry; check

lab.stretch: Run 1.1.0 in shadow instead: copy every request to it, return only 1.0.0's answer, and compare

sessions.label: Session 2
sessions.title: Rollback on evidence
sessions.summary: Rollback criteria written before the release, who decides, rolling back first and diagnosing second
outcomes: Apply written rollback criteria to a canary's metrics
Roll back within a time limit and record the evidence
Name the person accountable for the decision

lab.title: Roll back a faulty version
lab.summary: Trigger the rollback criteria with a seeded faulty version and roll back within five minutes.

steps.text: Read the criteria; start the canary of 1.2.0
Watch until a criterion fires
Roll back and time it
Find the cause; write the release log
Check

lab.stretch: Do the same rollback on the cluster with kubectl rollout undo and compare the time

sessions.label: Session 3
sessions.title: Drift in replayed traffic
sessions.summary: Data drift and concept drift, distribution tests and population stability, delayed labels and when drift should start a retraining
outcomes: Compute a drift statistic per feature against the training data
Name the shifted features and rule out a noisy one
Say what delayed labels allow you to conclude, and when

lab.title: Drift in four weeks
lab.summary: Replay four weeks of claims, compute a drift statistic per feature and name the shifted ones.

steps.text: Replay the four weeks through the service
Compute population stability and a KS test per feature
Name the shifted features; check the labels you have
Write the drift report; check

lab.stretch: Recompute the statistics with Evidently and compare its verdicts with yours

sessions.label: Session 4
sessions.title: Alerts and a runbook
sessions.summary: Alerts on symptoms the caller feels, durations that stop flapping, a runbook the on-call engineer can follow and the person who decides a rollback
outcomes: Write an alert rule on error ratio and one on latency
Test both rules against a recorded error spike
Write a one-page runbook with the accountable person

lab.title: Two alerts and a runbook
lab.summary: Write two alert rules and a one-page runbook for the on-call engineer, then choose the capstone model.

steps.text: Write the two rules without AI help
Test them on the recorded spike
Write the one-page runbook
Choose the capstone model; check

lab.stretch: Add a burn-rate alert on the error objective over two windows and test it on the same recording

days.label: Capstone
days.title: Capstone: a monitored service and its defence
days.subtitle: Eight minutes to show the service, four minutes of questions, and one fault injected by the assessor

capstone.summary: A model of the participant's choice taken to a monitored service, submitted as a public repository with container file, deployment manifests and dashboards as code, and a README reporting load-test results against a latency objective, a recorded canary release and rollback and a drift check, followed by an eight-minute defence and four minutes of questions
capstone.submission: A public GitHub repository link: the service with its container file, deployment manifests, dashboard and alert rules as code, and a README that reports the load-test results against a stated latency objective, the recorded canary release and rollback, and a drift check, with the command that produced each number.
